title.narrative: Integrated Cholera Response through Health and WASH Interventions in Gambella Woreda, Gambella Town and Itang Special Woreda of Gambella Regional State.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe Gambela Region of Ethiopia has been severely affected by recurrent cholera outbreaks due to limited access to clean water, poor sanitation, overcrowded living conditions, and frequent population movements. Recent reports indicate a surge in cholera cases, posing a significant public health risk. The outbreak, first detected in Akobo Woreda on February 11, 2025, has spread to 9 woredas and 4 refugee camps and resulted in 1787 cases and 32 deaths, indicating a Case Fatality Rate (CFR) of 1.79%, as per the regional Health Bureau and cluster report as of March 20, 2025. This project aims to provide an immediate and coordinated response to address the outbreak, reduce mortality, and prevent further spread in Gambela town, Gambela woreda, and Itang Special woreda of Gambela Regional State. Key activities of the project include providing support for case management and early investigation of outbreaks oral cholera mass vaccination campaigns capacity-building training for woreda healthcare workers equipping CTUs and ORPs with infection prevention supplies provision of personal protective equipment, essential medicine, and medical and WASH supplies and water treatment chemicals water quality testing kits construction/maintenance of sanitation and handwashing facilities at cholera treatment centers provision/distribution of lifesaving WASH NFIs and hygiene kits and WASH Social Behavior Change (SBC) messages and collaboration with regional health and water bureaus and partners. Considering the long-term presence in the area and having complementary projects, ASDEPO is committed to adding value in addressing the cholera response gaps with efficiency, effectiveness, and high-quality project outputs. ASDEPO is active in the health and WASH clusters at the national and sub-national levels. The coordination and reporting of project activities to the donor and the clusters via ActivityInfo will be strengthened. The project duration is 8 months. The total budget of the project is 319,280.00 USD. Through this budget, the project will directly reach 63,364 people in need in the targeted woredas, of whom 62% are female and 38% are male. Accountability for the Affected People (AAP) will be ensured through community feedback and compliant mechanisms that shall be ensured in each service area. This project aligns with the national cholera elimination plan and will contribute to addressing the immediate crisis and strengthening the health and WASH systems.lt/pgt
